newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Philips sees strong telecom sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Philips sees strong telecom sales.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV is seeing strong sales of its cellular phones China with an estimated five to 10 percent of market share, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"The market is estimated to be about six million cellular phones a year...we have about 5 to 10 percent of the China market," Mike McTighe, general director of Philips Consumer Communications (PCC), told Reuters in an interview.
McTighe was in Singapore to launch PCC's GSM phone factory and the Asia Telecom 1997 trade fair.
Cellular phones and other telephony products are a relatively new activity for the Dutch electronics giant. PCC, set up in January 1996, conducts the group's telecommunication activities.
PCC has grown rapidly registering growth rates of "200-300 percent" which should continue into 1998, McTighe said.
He declined to give details of revenues generated by PCC "due to competitive reasons" but said the division shipped about one million telephony products a month.
He said PCC employs 4,500 people worldwide, of which 3,000 have been with the company for less than a year. To get PCC started, the company managed to get "about 50 people from our competitors".

Total capital investment by PCC at its various manufacturing facilities at Le Mans in France, the United Kingdom, Hong Kong, Shenzhen in China, Fremont in the United States and in Singapore amounted to US$500 million, McTighe said.
The Singapore plant used to produce labour intensive audio and vision products but these are being phased out as PCC takes it over.
McTighe said the plant would be used solely for capital intensive telephony products by the end of 1998. Total capital investment to convert it was expected to be about US$100 million.

Other Asian markets where Philips cellular hand phones have made strong inroads include Australia. "We started in September 1996 with the Fizz (model) ... We have done extremely well in Australia and we are the number three brand there."

Mctighe said its cellular phones have done well in markets where Philips had a strong distribution network and where there was also strong brand recognition among consumers, as in Australia. "We don't do so well in the professional markets."
But its largest market in Asia was still Hong Kong and China, which account for half the group's cellular phone sales in the region.
"It is a premium market there. They want the highest level of performance, plenty of features and they need to be small."
McTighe said Philips would ship its latest model, the GSM Genie, said to be the world's lightest and smallest GSM phone from Singapore facility by the end of July.
